RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel doesn't show bias by itself, so it's weak evidence on its own. It becomes relevant context if other facts point the same way.

Your stronger argument is the comparison of qualifications. On paper, a PhD and eight years running a lab section look stronger than a master's degree and a management course. But "broad leadership experience" could be substantial, and you don't yet know how the panel weighted each criterion.

Your next step is to follow up in writing on the explanation you requested. Ask for the selection criteria and how each candidate was scored. In many jurisdictions applicants have a legal right to this. A refusal or a vague answer may shift the burden onto the employer.

Consult an equality ombudsman, union or employment lawyer soon, as deadlines may apply.
